newsitem.title: USA: Floods, soybeans crimp US cotton area - USDA analyst.
newsitem.headline: Floods, soybeans crimp US cotton area - USDA analyst.

text.p: U.S. cotton acreage would rise two percent in the Southeast this year but decline in California and the Delta, a USDA official said Monday.
U.S. acreage was pegged at 14.45 million acres, compared to 14.67 last year.

Flooding in the Tulare Basin of California contributed to an eight percent drop in acreage, to 1.075 million, said Ray Halley, chief of the crops branch of the National Agricultural Statistics Service.
Delta acreage, at 3.7 million, would drop six percent.
Louisiana led the region with a 25 percent drop with an equal amount of land moving into soybeans.
Mississippi was slated for a two percent drop and Arkansas, three percent. Both of those states had large increases in soybean acreage.
Cotton plantings in the Southeast would total 2.95 million acres, up two percent.
California was the only state with increased Pima plantings, up six percent to 175,000 acres. New Mexico would repeat last year's 14,000 acres while Texas and Arizona cut sharply.
